title: Scaling and storage
summary: Scale out without surprises: stateless services, load balancers, replicas, indexes and partitioning, and what each costs.

questions.prompt: Why do stateless application servers make horizontal scaling easy?
options: Any server can handle any request, so a load balancer can add or remove servers freely

questions.prompt: What's the main drawback of sticky sessions?
options: Load spreads unevenly and a server's failure loses its users' sessions

questions.prompt: Reads go to asynchronous read replicas. A user updates their profile and immediately sees the old one. Why?
options: Replication lag: the replica hasn't applied the write yet

questions.prompt: Adding an index on a column usually…
options: Speeds up reads that filter on it and slows down writes a little
Speeds up both reads and writes

questions.prompt: Orders are sharded by country. Most orders are from one country. What goes wrong?
options: One shard becomes a hot spot while others sit idle

questions.prompt: A payments ledger needs multi-row transactions and strong consistency. Which storage fits first?
True or false: vertical scaling (a bigger machine) is simple but eventually hits a hardware ceiling and leaves a single point of failure.
